safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of Type 2 diabetes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes diabetes but does not specify Type 2 as in Gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Recording diabetes without specifying Type 2 can reduce clinical usefulness of the problem list and may affect future medication choices, screening, and risk stratification (e.g., if later clinicians assume Type 1 vs Type 2). In this encounter it is unlikely to cause immediate harm because the presence of diabetes itself was captured.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a family history of Type 2 diabetes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated records family history of diabetes but does not specify Type 2.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Family history of diabetes is mainly used for long-term risk assessment and counseling; the specific type (Type 2) rarely changes acute management in this context. Capturing “family history of diabetes” without subtype is unlikely to lead to any direct clinical harm.

safety_verdicts.content: Prescribed a steroid cream to be used twice daily (BD).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes steroid cream but does not specify twice daily (BD) frequency.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the dosing frequency for a prescribed topical steroid can lead to underuse (treatment failure/prolonged symptoms) or overuse (skin atrophy, irritation), especially on hands with chronic exposure. This is most likely to cause delayed resolution or need for follow-up rather than severe injury.
